title: Blast Corps
subtitle: Rare · Nintendo 64
summary: Blast Corps is Rare's Nintendo 64 action-puzzle game about clearing a route for a runaway nuclear missile carrier. body: Blast Corps is Rare's Nintendo 64 action-puzzle game about clearing a route for a runaway nuclear missile carrier. Buildings and other obstacles must be removed before the vehicle reaches them, using a collection of demolition machines found around each location. The premise makes destruction an urgent practical task. A large building is a problem because it occupies the wrong place, and the player has to discover which machine can remove it quickly enough while the carrier continues moving towards it.

The bulldozer can ram structures, while other vehicles rely on sliding, dropping from a height or a robot's particular movement. Changing machines is essential when a route presents more than one kind of obstruction. Crates of explosives and other machinery add problems that require preparation before the last building can fall. The player studies the location as a sequence of jobs, deciding what should be moved or destroyed first and which useful vehicle needs to be waiting nearby when that task is complete.

After securing the carrier's route, the player can revisit a location to destroy remaining structures, activate lights and find secrets without the same immediate pressure. Medal targets and further challenges then turn that knowledge into faster, more accurate attempts. Developed by a small Rare team and released in 1997, Blast Corps found another use for the new console's three-dimensional worlds. The scenery becomes a working problem whose solution is visible in the empty space left behind when the appropriate machine has done its job.
